title.narrative: Efficient Transmission of Electricity from Renewable Energy Sources in Nepal

description.narrative: The general objective of the Project is to contribute to the sustainable economic and social development of Nepal and to the improvement of living conditions of the Nepali population (indirect contribution to the reduction of poverty, Millennium Development Goal (MDG) 1). Moreover, the Project will lead to global environmental and resource protection (MDG 7) via CO2e emission reductions, achieved by substituting emission-intensive fossil fuels for electricity production with climate-friendly electricity from hydropower.

description.narrative: Improved lowcarbon climate resilience (development)
Avoided carbon emissions per household

comment.narrative: No Baseline value is available and safely assumed 0 since the carbon emissions avoided are due to new connections to the electricity grid to be provided to households in the Trishuli River Basin

The Feasibility Study calculates for avoiding an average of 72 litre of kerosene per household per year approximately 209 kg of CO2 savings per household per year. Considering the households target is set at 2000 the Target in CO2 would amount to 209 2000 418000 kilograms 418 tonnes.

The value is to be interpreted as a cumulative one. As per the own LFIs words it would constitute a draft preliminary achievement based on the replacement of LPG liquefied petroleum gas consumption for electricity generation newly added ongrid connections in 602 households. Note that as per the LFIs inputs the unit of measurement is metric tons 31.40. It has been converted to tons for consistency across reported values. The reported value is inconsistent with the clarifications provided by the LFI 85 kg per household as that would amount to 51.17 tons instead of just 34.61. The intervention is aimed at improving access to electricity in the Trishuli River Basin north of Kathmandu by providing the transmission infrastructure to evacuate additional electricity for the regions hydropower plants.
